selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What scene are readers asked to imagine at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: They are asked to picture themselves in a time of ignorance and rough living, when people saw the world through unbelief, neglect, and a view of nature as lifeless.

questions.question: In that imagined setting, what effect do the Qur’anic verses have on a listener’s understanding of the world?
questions.answer: They transform the world from something dead and silent into something alive, aware, and engaged in praising Allah.

questions.question: What happens in the minds of the listeners when they hear that everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah?
questions.answer: The creatures they had thought dead or asleep seem to come alive, awaken, and begin reflecting Allah’s names.

questions.question: How is the sky described after the listener hears these verses?
questions.answer: It is presented like a mouth, with the stars acting like meaningful expressions that show wisdom and truth.

questions.question: How is the earth portrayed in this same image?
questions.answer: It is shown like a head, while land and sea are like tongues, and living things become expressions of glorification.

questions.question: Why would a person fail to fully appreciate the force of these verses?
questions.answer: A person would miss it if they only look at the verses as familiar teachings that everyone already knows instead of seeing how powerfully they first broke through darkness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does habit or over-familiarity do to a person’s reading of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It puts a thin but harmful cover over the verses, making their miracle and sweetness harder to feel.

questions.question: What specific aspect of the Qur’an is the reader being prepared to understand through this comparison?
questions.answer: The reader is being led to understand one of the highest levels of the Qur’an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the opening example about the Age of Ignorance?
questions.answer: It helps the reader feel how strongly the Qur’an changed people’s view of the universe.

questions.question: Before the light of the Qur’an is imagined as arriving, how is the world viewed?
questions.answer: It is viewed as covered by ignorance, neglect, and a sense that things are dead and controlled only by nature.

questions.question: What new understanding do the verses bring to the heavens and the earth?
questions.answer: They show that all creation is engaged in worship and points back to Allah.

questions.question: What change takes place in the listener rather than in creation itself?
questions.answer: The listener’s perception changes, so they begin to recognize life, meaning, and praise where they had not noticed it before.

questions.question: In the passage’s imagery, what role do the stars play?
questions.answer: They function like meaningful signs that express truth and wisdom.

questions.question: In the same imagery, what role do animals and plants play?
questions.answer: They are shown as if they are expressions of glorification spread across the earth.

questions.question: Why does the passage tell readers to look from the present back to that earlier time?
questions.answer: Because doing that helps them understand the original impact and beauty of the verses instead of taking them for granted.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens when Qur’anic verses become treated as ordinary and familiar?
questions.answer: Their power to break through darkness is no longer deeply felt or properly appreciated.

questions.question: What kind of darkness does the passage say the Qur’an’s verses remove?
questions.answer: They remove the darkness of unbelief, ignorance, and heedlessness.

questions.question: Why are the verses compared to shining stars?
questions.answer: Because they spread light, guide people, and break up spiritual darkness.

questions.question: What false impression about the world is challenged by the Qur’anic verses in the passage?
questions.answer: The false impression that the world is lifeless, empty of meaning, and disconnected from worship.

questions.question: When the verses are heard, how are creatures newly understood?
questions.answer: They are understood as active signs of Allah that glorify Him.

questions.question: What does the image of the sky as a mouth suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the heavens are not mute but are declaring meaning and pointing to Allah.

questions.question: What does the image of the earth with many tongues suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that different parts of the earth and its living things all express praise in their own ways.

questions.question: According to the passage, what blocks a person from tasting the sweetness of this miracle?
questions.answer: Looking through the filter of custom and shallow familiarity blocks that deeper appreciation.

questions.question: Why is historical imagination important for understanding these verses?
questions.answer: It helps readers recover the freshness and force those verses had when they first confronted a dark worldview.

title: Reviving Effect of Verses in the Age of Ignorance
